posts.text:
The Iran war magnified a long-running issue: US forward bases are easier to target than to defend, says Cato’s Evan Sankey. 

If forward bases can’t protect themselves or deter conflict, do they really serve US interests?

ow.ly/2max50YOILk

The jury was asked if Keith Pharms fired a weapon: it said no. But the judge sentenced him as if he did, doubling his sentence. Cato urges the Supreme Court to end sentencing based on acquitted conduct and restore the role of the jury. 
ow.ly/RoeX50YO36j

The public wants lower living costs. But that shouldn’t mean destructive gimmicks, price controls, or more subsidies. Politicians who reach for those tools will find they’ve bought themselves a news cycle and solved nothing, says Cato’s @MrRBourne. 

ow.ly/Ncpe50YOJQg

For 18 years, the NSA has collected Americans’ communications under FISA Section 702 with no probable cause warrant required. In this Cato Podcast episode, @PGEddington and @maria_sofia94 break down the latest reauthorization fight and what genuine reform would look like. 

Listen on Apple, Spotify, and our website! 
 
Apple: ow.ly/X6Iv50YOG4H  
Spotify: ow.ly/YElc50YOG4J  
Website: ow.ly/oP3350YOG4I

Trump's mortgage executive order identifies real problems with Dodd-Frank regulations, but no executive order can fix what Congress broke. Lasting reform means repealing harmful rules and ending federal subsidies that distort housing markets.

ow.ly/wjfz50YOefG

Section 122 is being used as a workaround to keep tariffs alive—even though it was built for a different era. Courts can’t fix this. Congress gave away its trade power, and it needs to take it back, says Cato's @clark_packard.

ow.ly/97Sw50YOeLI

Gas. Groceries. Rent. Childcare. High prices are hurting Americans everywhere — and Washington isn’t fixing it. 

Cato's new “Handbook on Affordability” offers 100+ better policy ideas to bring costs down sustainably.

The Supreme Court's rejection of Trump's emergency tariffs isn't just about trade. It's a check on the unconstrained executive power that every future president—left or right—would inherit, explains Cato’s @bskorup.

ow.ly/s4NJ50YOe03

The administration ramped up ICE arrests while slashing green card approvals, reports Cato’s @David_J_Bier. For relatives of US citizens stuck in the backlog, the delay can cause their legal status to lapse — making them deportable. 

ow.ly/5eIF50YObnt

Whether it’s obsolete programs from the Great Depression, or tax credits that colleges absorb through higher prices, there are better alternatives to improve policy and save taxpayers money.

Video
Every subsidy, every bailout, every "free" government program has a cost. Bastiat understood what too many politicians still pretend not to: the state has no money of its own. It only has yours.

Inspectors general cost just 0.06% of federal spending but identify tens of billions of dollars in waste every year. The Trump administration would cut IG budgets by 23% but that makes no sense especially because the administration itself has declared a "war on fraud", explains Cato's @CatoEdwards and @LettDominik.

ow.ly/S8Wv50YO8xX

CBP's new tariff refund system risks leaving thousands of American companies with far less than they're legally owed, Cato scholars warn. 

They break down the good, the bad, and what we still don't know: 
ow.ly/JSoE50YOf4W

AI isn’t just tech—it’s becoming an extension of our work, ideas, and livelihoods. 

That means it deserves strong protections from government overreach. The freedom to build, create, and innovate are especially important to safeguard. Learn more from @KevinTFrazier.
ow.ly/gT8J50YO2Jm

The FBI just conceded in court it did investigate the Cato Institute and its employees—after telling Cato in 2019 it had “no records.” Now the question is whether it’s still ongoing, as Congress debates FISA Section 702 and FBI surveillance powers, reports @PGEddington. ow.ly/s1Jr50YOeR3

There's strong evidence that rules-based monetary policy improves economic outcomes, says Cato's @JaiKedia. When the Fed follows a rule, the scope for political interference shrinks significantly.

Video

Our brains evolved for small-group, zero-sum competition—not vast markets among strangers. That mismatch helps explain why policies like rent control and tariffs stay popular despite poor economic results, argues Cato’s Adam Omary. 

ow.ly/ouvv50YO8hX
